scope: Read-only static SketchUp and hardware→machining→DXF audit

features.name: Real workshop catalog to native SketchUp furniture
features.assessment: Same persisted modules as React, typed parameter validation, remote layout and native component rendering exist. This is catalog projection, not proof of immutable published catalog release/version. Historical host fixtures are not current live-host proof.

features.name: Project binding, physical unit placement, duplication and publication
features.assessment: Connected model binding and server FurnitureInstance identity are implemented, with staged artifact publication. Legacy unconnected insertion retains local instanceRef. Current host undo/save-reopen/duplicate/publish proof remains unexecuted in this audit.

features.name: Dedicated device authentication
features.assessment: Device secret uses macOS Keychain or Windows credential vault; unsupported secure storage fails closed. Token held in memory and exchanged via device endpoint. OS host secure-store integration not exercised here.

features.name: Rich authoring resolve versus host editor
features.assessment: Versioned POST adapter exists but source-wide search finds no call site in plugin. User insert/edit executes GET layout. Hardware direct manipulation, machining inspect and preflight actions are explicitly disabled.

features.name: Hardware and relationship-derived machining
features.assessment: Authoring path has explicit relationships and compiled profile subset. Project path uses catalog machining and structural-role joinery rules. Neither proves arbitrary geometric-contact inference or a verified Blum SKU catalogue.

features.name: DXF cutplan geometry and drilling circles
features.assessment: 2D DXF layer-based output exists; rotated pieces lose drilling; depths and machine-specific programming are not encoded. No exact machine/software readback performed.

findings.title: Production drilling silently falls back to name-based heuristics and loses provenance in exports
findings.impact: A board named door/puerta can acquire two 35mm hinge holes without authoritative hardware. fallbackUsed/issues exist internally but are stripped from data.patterns consumed by DXF and production pack. Export failure also silently removes drilling and still reports successful DXF download.
findings.recommendation: Demo: label geometry-only exports and prohibit physical production from heuristic output. MVP: gate machining exports on explicit resolved operations and retain provenance/issues; separate preview inference from productive output.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

findings.title: DXF drilling omits rotated parts and per-hole depths
findings.impact: Rotated nested parts export contour without holes. Diameter/face layers cannot convey different depths for the same tool, and edge circles are projections not machine instructions.
findings.recommendation: Demo: use only verified unrotated sample as geometry preview. MVP: capability-gated adapter with explicit transform/depth semantics and exact import/readback dossier.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

findings.title: Generic fallback can replace native resolved geometry on nil layout parameter edit
findings.impact: RemoteCatalogProvider is primary; Application injects StaticCatalogProvider as its fallback. On a fallback/error path returning nil layout (not normal successful remote resolution), update_furniture blocks nil layout only for material changes; a parameter-only update can clear native children and build generic boards. This is a statically reachable conditional risk, not a live-host reproduction.
findings.recommendation: Demo: require online resolve and fixed prepared fixture. MVP: preserve accepted geometry for all unavailable/incompatible responses; restrict generic rendering to explicitly separate preview state and route edits through shared coordinator.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

findings.title: Rich authoring and machining user interaction remains disconnected
findings.impact: Resolver presence does not mean operator can move a shelf/hardware and see authoritative drilling update. Every hardware edit and manufacturing/preflight action is disabled in CapabilityPolicy.
findings.recommendation: Demo: show preconfigured placement, not arbitrary hardware authoring. MVP: one end-to-end accepted snapshot edit with correlation, supersession, rollback, undo, preflight and real host proof.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

findings.title: Machining truth is fragmented between compiled authoring profiles and catalog-driven project exports
findings.impact: Authoring accepts only two explicit hinge-code patterns while catalog engine supports hardware.machining. Unknown authoring hardware profile emits no drilling. Same commercial hardware may therefore yield different results by route; arbitrary real brand support is unproven.
findings.recommendation: Demo: exact curated codes and explicit patterns. MVP: a single versioned SKU/pattern authority consumed across resolve/preflight/export; unknown productive pattern blocks rather than guessing.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

findings.title: Catalog cache is not automatically revalidated and failure retains prior cache
findings.impact: Normal reads return cached contract without TTL/session-key comparison. A failed forced refresh marks status but leaves prior cache available to next normal read. Definition list version is not an immutable manufacturing revision guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Demo: explicit refresh before session and stop on auth/catalog errors. MVP: tenant/session keyed cache, stale status and accepted catalog revision, blocked mutation until authoritative revalidation.
findings.proof: Code path inspected; no live host or machine execution.

integration.break: Immutable published catalog lifecycle not established by this projection; POST authoring is unused in current edit interaction.
integration.demo: Curated catalog fixture, live online resolve, manually verify host save/reopen and undo.

chain: Hardware catalog / structural role or explicit relationship
Go compiled authoring machining OR TS project catalog machining
integration.break: No single common end-to-end authoritative pipeline; not arbitrary physical contact-based automatic machining.
integration.demo: Only known fixture relationship and named technical pattern; no Blum product claim without real SKU evidence.

integration.break: Heuristic provenance lost, errors swallowed, rotated drilling omitted, no machine readback.
integration.demo: Geometry visualization only; controlled exact-machine pilot needed before production.

unknowns: No live SketchUp host run, TestUp session, real Keychain/Vault interaction, interactive undo/redo or save/reopen was executed by this subtask.
No exact machine model/control/software, import/readback, operator sign-off or checksum evidence was supplied.
No verified physical Blum SKU data/model/pattern was inspected; BIS-CL110 is a repository code, not proof of manufacturer interoperability.
No claim of generated-contract parity from source inspection alone; central parent test evidence must be attached separately.

benchmarks.problem: Hardware selection linked to cabinet planning
benchmarks.learn: Product SKU and technical pattern must travel together.
benchmarks.doNotCopy: Do not claim its product breadth or BXF compatibility.
benchmarks.adapt: Curated verifiable SKU/pattern list for a narrow demo.

benchmarks.how: Maestro lab/cnc and DXF import workflows
benchmarks.learn: Import is only a step; exact software readback is required.
benchmarks.doNotCopy: Do not build enterprise CAM or invent a postprocessor.
benchmarks.adapt: Machine dossier plus one exact controlled import/readback.

benchmarks.doNotCopy: Never derive business identity from host component identity.
benchmarks.adapt: Keep per-furniture isolation and server-owned IDs, verify make_unique/undo/save-reopen in host.
